body:
## Goal

Extend the local usage dashboard beyond OpenCode so it can compare usage across coding-agent tools.

This is the umbrella issue for the shared dashboard/data-model work. Tool-specific source adapters are split into separate issues so Codex and Hermes can be implemented and validated independently.

## Split implementation issues

- #3 — Add Codex usage source adapter
- #4 — Add Hermes usage source adapter

## Current baseline

- OpenCode usage from `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is the active source.
- PR #2 prepares the dashboard framing/UI for cross-tool usage but does not implement Codex or Hermes source adapters.

## Proposed product shape

Add a tool dimension to the data model and UI:

- Tool filter: OpenCode / Codex / Hermes / All tools
- Per-tool overview cards: sessions, total tokens, input tokens, output tokens
- Daily stacked chart grouped by top N model/tool series, with long tail grouped as Other
- Model breakdown table with tool, provider, model, sessions, total/input/output tokens
- Usage history table with tool, date, model, title/session summary, tokens

## Design notes

- Keep colors categorical and position-based in charts, not hardcoded per model, because the top models can vary by date range and tool.
- Keep long-tail series grouped into Other after top 6-8 visible series.
- Treat cache/cost as secondary unless explicitly selected.
- Avoid claiming parity across tools until the local data quality is verified for each source.
- Do not silently treat missing/unavailable tool data as zero usage.

## Implementation notes

Use a source adapter layer:

```text
sources/
  opencode.py
  codex.py   # tracked by #3
  hermes.py  # tracked by #4
```

Each adapter should normalize into a common record shape:

```text
tool, session_id, timestamp, title, provider, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read, cache_write
```

## Acceptance criteria

- Dashboard can show OpenCode-only exactly as today.
- Shared data model supports multiple tools without breaking existing OpenCode metrics.
- Missing/unavailable Codex or Hermes data is shown clearly, not silently treated as zero usage.
- Chart and table order stay consistent: same top-N order, same position colors, Other muted gray.
- Validation documents where each tool's data came from and which metrics are trustworthy.
- Codex implementation is tracked separately in #3.
- Hermes implementation is tracked separately in #4.
title: Add cross-tool usage dashboard with split source adapters
